title: Ninth Word Fourth Point Conclusion On Obligatory Prayer And Its Times

questions.question: What does the early morning after night make a person think about?
questions.answer: It makes a person think about the rising again after death.

questions.question: How sure is that rising compared with a new morning after night?
questions.answer: It is just as sure.

questions.question: What else is said to be just as sure after the middle life between death and rising?
questions.answer: The new life that comes like spring is just as sure.

questions.question: What do the five daily prayer times begin?
questions.answer: They begin important changes.

questions.question: Besides big changes, what else do these times help people remember?
questions.answer: They help people remember other great changes too.

questions.question: Through the events Allah brings each day, what do these times remind people of in the year?
questions.answer: They remind people of Allah’s power and mercy shown again and again through the year.

questions.question: What do these times also remind people of across long stretches of time?
questions.answer: They remind people of Allah’s signs in every age and time period.

questions.question: According to the passage, what are the required prayers like for people?
questions.answer: They are a natural duty, the foundation of worship, and something owed.

questions.question: Why are the required prayers very suitable for these times?
questions.answer: Because these times carry great reminders, so prayer fits them very well.

questions.question: What morning is compared to the morning after this night?
questions.answer: The morning of resurrection is compared to it.

questions.question: If a child knows morning comes after night, what does the passage say that should teach us?
questions.answer: It should teach us that rising again is also certain.

questions.question: What season is mentioned after the middle world between death and resurrection?
questions.answer: Spring is mentioned.

questions.question: Are the five prayer times shown as random parts of the day or meaningful times?
questions.answer: They are shown as meaningful times.

questions.question: What kind of things does each prayer time mark the start of?
questions.answer: The start of important changes.

questions.question: What does Allah’s power during each day make people remember?
questions.answer: It makes people remember His mighty works and His mercy.

questions.question: In what three bigger circles of time do these reminders appear?
questions.answer: In each year, each age, and each epoch.

questions.question: What does the passage say the set prayers are the basis of?
questions.answer: They are the basis of worship.

questions.question: What does the passage say people owe regarding these prayers?
questions.answer: These prayers are a clear debt people owe.

questions.question: What future morning does the second morning bring to mind?
questions.answer: It brings to mind the morning of resurrection.

questions.question: How certain is resurrection said to be?
questions.answer: It is as certain as morning coming after night.

questions.question: What comes after the Intermediate Realm like spring comes after winter?
questions.answer: A new spring-like life comes after it.

questions.question: What is one thing each of the five times does?
questions.answer: Each one starts an important turning point.

questions.question: What is another thing each of the five times does?
questions.answer: Each one reminds people of other great turning points.

questions.question: Whose power is shown in the daily events at these times?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is shown.

questions.question: What two things do these times remind people about from Allah?
questions.answer: They remind people of His power and His mercy.

questions.question: Are the required prayers presented as optional extras or as something deeply fitting?
questions.answer: They are presented as deeply fitting.

questions.question: Give one reason the required prayers are deeply fitting at these times.
questions.answer: These times are full of reminders, so worship belongs in them.

questions.question: When a new day begins after darkness, what bigger event should that remind us of?
questions.answer: It should remind us of the day people are raised again.

questions.question: What point is made by comparing morning after night with resurrection?
questions.answer: The point is that resurrection is not doubtful; it is certain.

questions.question: What image is used for what follows the Intermediate Realm?
questions.answer: The image of spring is used.

questions.question: How many daily times are being talked about in this passage?
questions.answer: Five times.

questions.question: What do these five times have in common?
questions.answer: They all begin important changes and remind people of other great changes.

questions.question: What do the daily workings of Allah at these times call to mind?
questions.answer: They call to mind His wonderful acts of power and His gifts of mercy.

questions.question: Do these reminders only point to one day, or also to longer times?
questions.answer: They also point to longer times.

questions.question: Name the longer times mentioned.
questions.answer: The year, the age, and the epoch.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: It describes them as natural, basic to worship, and truly owed.

questions.question: What does the passage say the next morning helps people remember?
questions.answer: It helps them remember resurrection morning.

questions.question: Which is said to be equally certain: sunrise after night or resurrection?
questions.answer: Both are said to be equally certain.

questions.question: What living season is linked with what comes after the Intermediate Realm?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: Why are the five prayer times important in this passage?
questions.answer: Because each one begins a great change and reminds us of others.

questions.question: What can a Muslim learn from these daily times about Allah?
questions.answer: A Muslim can learn about Allah’s great power and mercy.

questions.question: Do the times remind people only of miracles of power, or also of loving gifts?
questions.answer: They remind people of both mighty power and merciful gifts.

questions.question: Over what repeating time cycle do these reminders happen again and again?
questions.answer: They happen through every year.

questions.question: Over what larger stretches beyond a year do they also happen?
questions.answer: Through every age and every epoch.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage make about praying at these times?
questions.answer: It says the required prayers fit these times perfectly.

questions.question: After one night ends, what greater morning should come to mind?
questions.answer: The morning when people are brought back to life.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about being sure of that day?
questions.answer: We should be as sure of it as we are sure morning will come.

questions.question: What is compared to spring after the Intermediate Realm?
questions.answer: The life that comes after it is compared to spring.

questions.question: What do all five prayer times announce at the start?
questions.answer: They announce important new turnings.

questions.question: What do they also help the heart remember?
questions.answer: They help the heart remember other great turnings too.

questions.question: What in everyday life causes these reminders to happen?
questions.answer: Allah’s mighty daily actions cause them.

questions.question: What kinds of signs do these times point to again and again?
questions.answer: They point to signs of divine power and signs of mercy.

questions.question: In what lengths of time are these signs seen?
questions.answer: In each year, each age, and each epoch.

questions.question: Why is it right to pray the prescribed prayers at those times?
questions.answer: Because prayer belongs at times filled with such strong reminders, and those prayers are a duty owed to Allah.
